mstts:express-as.prosody: Hey there—welcome to a journey where we get to imagine what work and ownership could look like if we turned tradition on its head. Have you ever wondered what might happen if regular people—not just executives or shareholders—actually called the shots in their workplaces? Together, we're about to explore the world of worker cooperatives, those remarkable spaces where collective ownership and economic democracy aren't just buzzwords, but lived realities. Inspired by the questions asked in Chris Wright’s book, Worker Cooperatives and Revolution: History and Possibilities in the United States, we're going to trace the roots of these worker-owned enterprises—from their earliest beginnings to the vibrant movements shaping them today. Along the way, we'll see how these cooperatives became much more than just a way to make a living. They became testing grounds for social change, places where people found both security and a sense of purpose, and where the struggle for economic justice met real-world challenges. As we move through stories of grassroots organizing, political pushback, and bold dreams for the future, you'll get to see the power and the pitfalls of building something new in a world stacked in favor of the status quo. So, get ready to rethink what’s possible—because together, we're about to open up new ways of seeing work, ownership, and the kind of future we can create when we come together.
